page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-32GB is a Cloud Native family server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 16 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 1.0 thread per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, configured with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or a dedicated GPU, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show a mix of performance tiers. The server demonstrates strong single-core performance in Geekbench with a score of 2197.0, and top-tier text processing capabilities at 2941.0. However, stress-ng single-core CPU performance is categorized in the bottom 10% at 785.99, while multi-core performance is average at 10921.94. Memory bandwidth presents a bottleneck, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 25% at 24.65 GB/sec and 19.33 GB/sec respectively, though cached small-block reads perform at an average rate of 1073.93 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds are average for prompt processing but drop to a poor 4.74 tokens/sec for 7B model text generation.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a cost-effective option for workloads that require high core counts but can tolerate shared resource density. It is suitable for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, text processing, and static web serving, where its average multi-core and database operation benchmarks align with resource availability. It is less suited for memory-intensive operations or sustained high-performance single-core computing due to its shared CPU model and weak uncached memory bandwidth.
